The primary projector GUI now contains only global presentation controls, power status and the removable Projection Core.
Use Image Workspace, Item Workspace or Entity Workspace to choose and edit the content being projected.
Apply saves global Scale, Lift, Rotation, Floating, Lighting, Ghost Effect and Tint. Source workspaces save their own content directly.
This handbook is temporary development documentation and is intentionally updated as systems become usable.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.core.5: Netherite: 384 PU · scale 160px · lift 160px · float 32px. The chassis can still impose a lower geometric limit.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.1: Import normalized PNG, JPG, JPEG or WebP assets. The server stores normalized PNG assets by SHA-256 ID.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.2: Current plane chassis expose Front and Back. Back may mirror Front, show Front readable, or use an independent image.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.3: Vertical Flip and Scanlines are image-specific controls and therefore live in this workspace instead of the primary GUI.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.4: Mirage Prism now stores independent North/East/South/West image faces. Same Source on All Faces copies North's asset reference without duplicating files.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.item.1: Click an item onto the virtual Snapshot slot. Mirage copies one serialized visual snapshot and never removes the real item.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.item.2: Blocks render as 3D blocks, ordinary items use their full 3D item model, and standalone armor targets equipped geometry on the invisible rig.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.item.3: Clearing the virtual slot deletes only the snapshot. There is no obtainable stored item to steal or duplicate.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.1: Craft an Empty Scan Template with paper surrounded by eight iron nuggets, then Shift + right-click one living entity or player. Mirage gives this deliberate scan gesture priority over the target interaction.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.2: Humanoid scans expose Head, Chest, Legs, Feet, Main Hand and Off Hand incoming/projected channels. Each conflict is resolved slot by slot.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.3: Horse scans expose Saddle and Body Armor channels. Generic entities keep unsupported visual equipment inside the frozen entity snapshot.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.4: Humanoid projections have persistent pose presets. Pose changes the virtual rig only; scanned body and equipment snapshots stay untouched.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.5: Pose-aware preview fitting and conservative clearance reserve extra room for raised or spread arms.
Scale preserves the source aspect/model proportions. Lift moves the lowest projected point above the emitter.
Rotation controls period, direction and orientation. Floating controls amplitude and either time-cycle or rotation-synced timing.
Ghost Effect changes transparency. Tint applies a hologram color multiplier. Fullbright ignores world light.
Projection Power and clearance must both pass. Debug chassis override is Creative-only and never bypasses Core limits.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.title: Development / Known Boundaries
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.1: Prism is functional for static Image faces. Effigy and Colossal remain future chassis contracts, while Wide/Tall/Field still need their multi-source layout pass.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.2: Optional backpack/accessory/artifact integrations are outside the base scope and will be adapters after the core systems stabilize.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.3: Humanoid pose presets are implemented. Special renderer compatibility and exact species-aware Entity bounds still need refinement.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.4: If a renderer cannot safely support a feature, Mirage should fall back rather than silently corrupt shared render state.

handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.6: Mounted/composite scans such as jockeys remain excluded until composite projections are designed.
